newsitem.title: USA: Ralston withdraws over adultery - officials.
newsitem.headline: Ralston withdraws over adultery - officials.

text.p: Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston on Monday withdrew himself from consideration to become chairman of the U.S. military Joint Chiefs of Staff because of an uproar over an adulterous affair he had 13 years ago, defense officials said.

"He did not want to, but he has decided to withdraw," said one official, who asked not to be identified, several hours after Ralston discussed the issue privately with Defense Secretary William Cohen.
Ralston, 53, the vice chairman of the joint chiefs, admitted last week that he had an adulterous relationship while separated from his first wife more than a decade ago.
He was expected to issue a statement later explaining why he decided not to fight to remain in consideration to succeed Army Gen. John Shalikashvili in the nation's top military job.
Members of Congress had warned after the controversy broke that the Senate might reject Ralston if he were to be nominated by President Bill Clinton for the joint chiefs' leadership.
